answer: Pin each identity to a distinct network location: several independent verifiers measure round-trip latency to the agent and triangulate where it really sits, so the timing signal must match one physical machine in one region. A sybil farm running dozens of clones on one server betrays itself with near-identical latency fingerprints, like many nests crowded into a single willow. Cloning then costs a separate machine and network in every region faked, while a lone sparrow of a real agent passes cheaply because its timing is naturally unique.
